title: Definition of the State
text: In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires, 'the State' includes the Government and Parliament of India and the Government and the Legislature of each of the States and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.
plain_language: Defines 'the State' as any government body, parliament, state legislature, or local authority that must respect your fundamental rights.

title: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of fundamental rights - Pre-constitutional laws
text: All laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution, in so far as they are inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.
plain_language: Any law made before the Constitution came into effect becomes invalid if it violates your fundamental rights.

title: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of fundamental rights - Post-constitutional laws
text: The State shall not make any law which takes away or abridges the rights conferred by this Part and any law made in contravention of this clause shall, to the extent of the contravention, be void.
plain_language: The government cannot pass new laws that take away or reduce your fundamental rights.

title: Equality before law and equal protection of laws
text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
plain_language: Everyone is equal in the eyes of the law, and the government must protect everyone equally.
landmark_cases: E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu (1974) - Introduced the 'new doctrine' of Article 14, establishing that equality is antithetical to arbitrariness.

title: Prohibition of discrimination - Non-discrimination by the State
text: The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them.
plain_language: The government cannot discriminate against you based on your religion, race, caste, gender, or place of birth.

title: Prohibition of discrimination - Equal access to public places
text: No citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them, be subject to any disability, liability, restriction or condition with regard to access to shops, public restaurants, hotels and places of public entertainment; or the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads and places of public resort maintained wholly or partly out of State funds or dedicated to the use of the general public.
plain_language: No citizen can be barred from using public places like shops, restaurants, roads, or public wells based on religion, race, caste, gender, or birth place.

title: Equality of opportunity in public employment - General rule
text: There shall be equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.
plain_language: Every citizen has an equal chance to apply for and get a government job.

title: Equality of opportunity in public employment - Non-discrimination
text: No citizen shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them, be ineligible for, or discriminated against in respect of, any employment or office under the State.
plain_language: You cannot be denied a government job or discriminated against based on your religion, caste, gender, lineage, or residence.

title: Abolition of Untouchability
text: 'Untouchability' is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The enforcement of any disability arising out of 'Untouchability' shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.
plain_language: Practicing untouchability in any form is completely banned and is a punishable crime.

title: Abolition of titles - State prohibition
text: No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State.
plain_language: The government cannot grant nobility or aristocratic titles to citizens, except for military and academic honors.

title: Abolition of titles - Foreign titles prohibition
text: No citizen of India shall accept any title from any foreign State.
plain_language: Indian citizens are not allowed to accept titles or nobility honors from foreign countries.

title: Abolition of titles - Foreign titles for non-citizens in State service
text: No person who is not a citizen of India shall, while he holds any office of profit or trust under the State, accept without the consent of the President any title from any foreign State.
plain_language: A non-citizen holding a government job or position of trust in India cannot accept a title from a foreign country without the President's permission.

title: Abolition of titles - Foreign gifts and offices for officeholders
text: No person holding any office of profit or trust under the State shall, without the consent of the President, accept any present, emolument, or office of any kind from or under any foreign State.
plain_language: Anyone holding a government job or position of trust cannot accept gifts, payments, or positions from a foreign country without the President's permission.

title: Right to freedom of speech and expression
text: All citizens shall have the right to freedom of speech and expression.
plain_language: You have the right to freely express your ideas, opinions, and views through speech, writing, or media.
landmark_cases: Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras (1950) - Held that freedom of speech includes freedom of propagation and circulation of ideas.

title: Right to assemble peaceably and without arms
text: All citizens shall have the right to assemble peaceably and without arms.
plain_language: You can gather peacefully in public groups as long as no one carries weapons.

title: Right to form associations, unions, or co-operative societies
text: All citizens shall have the right to form associations or unions or co-operative societies.
plain_language: You have the right to start or join organizations, trade unions, clubs, or cooperative groups.

title: Right to move freely throughout the territory of India
text: All citizens shall have the right to move freely throughout the territory of India.
plain_language: You can travel anywhere you want across India without restrictions.

title: Right to reside and settle in any part of India
text: All citizens shall have the right to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India.
plain_language: You are free to live, buy a home, or settle down in any state or region of India.

title: Right to practise any profession, or carry on trade or business
text: All citizens shall have the right to practise any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade or business.
plain_language: You can choose any lawful job, career, business, or trade to earn a living.

title: Protection in respect of conviction - Protection against ex post facto laws
text: No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.
plain_language: You cannot be punished for an act if it was not illegal at the exact time you did it, nor can you be given a harsher penalty than what was set by law then.

title: Protection in respect of conviction - Protection against double jeopardy
text: No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.
plain_language: You cannot be put on trial and punished twice for the exact same crime.

title: Protection in respect of conviction - Protection against self-incrimination
text: No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.
plain_language: If accused of a crime, you cannot be forced by authorities to confess or give evidence against yourself.

title: Protection of life and personal liberty
text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
plain_language: You cannot be arrested or have your freedom or life taken away except through a fair legal process.
landmark_cases: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) - Expanded 'personal liberty' to mean procedures must be just, fair, and reasonable, establishing life with dignity.
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) - Unanimously affirmed that the Right to Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21.

title: Right to education
text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.
plain_language: Every child between the ages of 6 and 14 has a right to receive free and compulsory education from the government.

title: Protection against arrest - Right to grounds of arrest and legal counsel
text: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice.
plain_language: If arrested, police must tell you why you are being detained and allow you to hire a lawyer of your choice.

title: Protection against arrest - Right to production before magistrate within 24 hours
text: Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate and no such person shall be detained in custody beyond the said period without the authority of a magistrate.
plain_language: The police must bring an arrested person before a judge within 24 hours, or let them go.

title: Protection against arrest - Exceptions for enemy aliens and preventive detention
text: Nothing in clauses (1) and (2) shall apply—(a) to any person who for the time being is an enemy alien; or (b) to any person who is arrested or detained under any law providing for preventive detention.
plain_language: The rights to be informed of the arrest reason and produced before a magistrate within 24 hours do not apply to enemy aliens or people held under preventive detention laws.

title: Protection against arrest - Maximum period for preventive detention without Advisory Board review
text: No law providing for preventive detention shall authorise the detention of a person for a longer period than three months unless an Advisory Board consisting of persons who are, or have been, or are qualified to be appointed as, Judges of a High Court has reported before the expiration of the said period of three months that there is in its opinion sufficient cause for such detention.
plain_language: A person cannot be held under preventive detention for more than three months unless an Advisory Board (made up of people qualified to be High Court judges) reviews the case and finds sufficient cause to continue the detention.

title: Protection against arrest - Right to be informed of grounds and make representation
text: When any person is detained in pursuance of an order made under any law providing for preventive detention, the authority making the order shall, as soon as may be, communicate to such person the grounds on which the order has been made and shall afford him the earliest opportunity of making a representation against the order.
plain_language: If you are preventively detained, the authorities must tell you why as soon as possible and give you an early chance to challenge the detention order.

title: Protection against arrest - Authority may withhold facts against public interest
text: Nothing in clause (5) shall require the authority making any such order as is referred to in that clause to disclose facts which such authority considers to be against the public interest to disclose.
plain_language: The government does not have to reveal every detail behind a preventive detention order if it believes disclosing that information would harm the public interest.

title: Protection against arrest - Parliament's power to legislate on preventive detention procedure
text: Parliament may by law prescribe the circumstances under which, and the class or classes of cases in which, a person may be detained for a period longer than three months under any law providing for preventive detention without obtaining the opinion of an Advisory Board, the maximum period for which any person may in any class or classes of cases be detained under any law providing for preventive detention, and the procedure to be followed by an Advisory Board in an inquiry.
plain_language: Parliament can pass laws that set out when someone can be detained beyond three months without an Advisory Board's opinion, the maximum detention period allowed, and the procedure the Advisory Board must follow.

title: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
text: Traffic in human beings and beggar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.
plain_language: Human trafficking, forced unpaid labor, and modern slavery are strictly prohibited and illegal.

title: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour - State's power to impose compulsory service
text: Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from imposing compulsory service for public purposes, and in imposing such service the State shall not make any discrimination on grounds only of religion, race, caste or class or any of them.
plain_language: The government can require compulsory public service (like military conscription or disaster relief work), but it cannot discriminate based on religion, race, caste, or class when doing so.

title: Prohibition of employment of children in factories and hazardous work
text: No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment.
plain_language: Children under 14 years old are legally banned from working in factories, mines, or dangerous jobs.

title: Freedom of conscience and right to profess, practise and propagate religion
text: Subject to public order, morality and health and to the other provisions of this Part, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion.
plain_language: You have full freedom to follow, practice, and share any religion you choose, or follow no religion at all.

title: Freedom of religion - State's power to regulate secular activity associated with religion
text: Nothing in this article shall affect the operation of any existing law or prevent the State from making any law regulating or restricting any economic, financial, political or other secular activity which may be associated with religious practice.
plain_language: The government can regulate the non-religious, secular side of religious practices, such as the economic or financial or political activities that happen alongside them.

title: Freedom of religion - State's power to provide for social welfare, reform, and opening of Hindu religious institutions
text: Nothing in this article shall affect the operation of any existing law or prevent the State from making any law providing for social welfare and reform or the throwing open of Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all classes and sections of Hindus.
plain_language: The government can pass laws for social reform and welfare, including opening up public Hindu temples and religious institutions to all Hindus regardless of caste or class.

title: Freedom to manage religious affairs
text: Subject to public order, morality and health, every religious denomination or any section thereof shall have the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes; to manage its own affairs in matters of religion; to own and acquire movable and immovable property; and to administer such property in accordance with law.
plain_language: Religious groups have the right to set up places of worship, manage their own religious matters, and own property.

title: Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion
text: No person shall be compelled to pay any taxes, the proceeds of which are specifically appropriated in payment of expenses for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion or religious denomination.
plain_language: The government cannot force you to pay taxes to promote or maintain any specific religion.

title: Freedom as to religious instruction in State-funded educational institutions
text: No religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
plain_language: Schools and colleges entirely funded by the government cannot teach religious courses.

title: Freedom as to religious instruction - Exception for endowed or trust-based institutions administered by the State
text: Nothing in clause (1) shall apply to an educational institution which is administered by the State but has been established under any endowment or trust which requires that religious instruction shall be imparted in such institution.
plain_language: If the State runs a school that was originally set up by an endowment or trust requiring religious teaching, that school is allowed to continue giving religious instruction.

title: Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or worship - Consent requirement
text: No person attending any educational institution recognised by the State or receiving aid out of State funds shall be required to take part in any religious instruction that may be imparted in such institution or to attend any religious worship that may be conducted in such institution or in any premises attached thereto unless such person or, if such person is a minor, his guardian has given his consent thereto.
plain_language: Students at State-recognized or State-aided schools cannot be forced to take part in religious instruction or worship unless they (or their guardian, if they're a minor) have given consent.

title: Protection of minorities - Right to conserve distinct language, script or culture
text: Any section of the citizens residing in the territory of India or any part thereof having a distinct language, script or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same.
plain_language: Minority groups have the protected right to preserve their unique language, alphabet, and cultural traditions.

title: Protection of minorities - Non-discrimination in educational institution admissions
text: No citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language or any of them.
plain_language: No state-funded educational institution can reject your admission based solely on your religion, caste, race, or language.

title: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
text: All minorities, whether based on religion or language, shall have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
plain_language: Religious and linguistic minorities have the right to set up and run their own schools and colleges.

title: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions - Fair compensation on compulsory acquisition of property
text: In making any law providing for the compulsory acquisition of any property of an educational institution established and administered by a minority, referred to in clause (1), the State shall ensure that the amount fixed by or determined under such law for the acquisition of such property is such as would not restrict or abrogate the right guaranteed under that clause.
plain_language: If the government compulsorily acquires property belonging to a minority-run educational institution, it must pay an amount that does not undermine the minority's right to run that institution.

title: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions - Non-discrimination in State aid
text: The State shall not, in granting aid to educational institutions, discriminate against any educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether based on religion or language.
plain_language: The government cannot deny or reduce funding to a school or college just because it is run by a religious or linguistic minority.

title: Remedies for enforcement of rights - Right to move Supreme Court
text: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed.
plain_language: You have a direct right to approach the Supreme Court if your fundamental rights are violated.
landmark_cases: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) - Established the 'Basic Structure Doctrine', holding Judicial Review under Article 32 as unamendable.

title: Remedies for enforcement of rights - Power of Supreme Court to issue writs
text: The Supreme Court shall have power to issue directions or orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, whichever may be appropriate, for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by this Part.
plain_language: The Supreme Court can issue binding legal orders (writs) to protect citizens when their fundamental rights are broken.

title: Remedies for enforcement of rights - Parliament's power to empower other courts
text: Without prejudice to the powers conferred on the Supreme Court by clauses (1) and (2), Parliament may by law empower any other court to exercise within the local limits of its jurisdiction all or any of the powers exercisable by the Supreme Court under clause (2).
plain_language: Parliament can pass a law allowing other courts to exercise the same writ powers as the Supreme Court, within their local jurisdiction.

title: Remedies for enforcement of rights - Right cannot be suspended except as provided by the Constitution
text: The right guaranteed by this article shall not be suspended except as otherwise provided for by this Constitution.
plain_language: The right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights cannot be taken away, except in situations the Constitution itself allows (such as during a national emergency).

title: Preamble to the Constitution of India
text: WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and to secure to all its citizens: JUSTICE, social, economic and political; LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation; IN OUR CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949, do HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION.
plain_language: The foundational pledge outlining India as an independent, equal, and democratic republic ensuring justice, freedom, equality, and unity for all its people.

title: Policy principles - Right to adequate means of livelihood
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the citizens, men and women equally, have the right to an adequate means of livelihood.
plain_language: The government should work to ensure both men and women have fair ways to earn a decent living.

title: Policy principles - Ownership and control of material resources for common good
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good.
plain_language: Public resources should be managed and shared to benefit the entire community rather than just a few.

title: Policy principles - Prevention of concentration of wealth
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment.
plain_language: The government should structure the economy so that wealth does not get trapped in the hands of a few rich individuals.

title: Policy principles - Equal pay for equal work for men and women
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
plain_language: Men and women doing the exact same work should be paid equal wages.

title: Policy principles - Health and strength of workers and protection of children
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the health and strength of workers, men and women, and the tender age of children are not abused.
plain_language: Workers should not be forced into dangerous jobs that ruin their health, and children must be protected from work exploitation.

title: Policy principles - Healthy development opportunities for children
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner and in conditions of freedom and dignity.
plain_language: The state should ensure children grow up in safe, dignified conditions with healthy opportunities.

title: Right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall, within the limits of its economic capacity and development, make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, and in other cases of undeserved want.
plain_language: The government should try its best to provide jobs, education, and welfare support for the elderly, sick, disabled, or unemployed.

title: Uniform civil code for the citizens
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India.
plain_language: The state should work toward creating a single unified civil law for personal matters like marriage and inheritance for all citizens across India.

title: Provision for early childhood care and education to children below six years
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
plain_language: The government should aim to provide early childhood daycare, health care, and preschool education for kids under 6.

title: Promotion of educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and weaker sections
part: Part IV - Directive Principles of State Policy
text: The State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, and shall protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation.
plain_language: The government must actively protect disadvantaged communities like SCs and STs from social unfairness and boost their education and job opportunities.

title: Fundamental Duty - Abide by Constitution and respect Flag and Anthem
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
plain_language: As a citizen, you must follow constitutional rules and show respect to the Indian Flag and National Anthem.

title: Fundamental Duty - Cherish ideals of the freedom struggle
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
plain_language: You should honor and remember the patriotic values that guided India's freedom fighters.

title: Fundamental Duty - Uphold sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.
plain_language: You are duty-bound to protect the unity, oneness, and independence of India.

title: Fundamental Duty - Defend the country and render national service
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
plain_language: You should be prepared to defend the nation and offer national service whenever called upon.

title: Fundamental Duty - Promote harmony, brotherhood, and respect dignity of women
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
plain_language: You must promote harmony across different religions and regions, and reject any practice that disrespects women.

title: Fundamental Duty - Value and preserve composite culture
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
plain_language: You should appreciate and help protect India's diverse cultural traditions and history.

title: Fundamental Duty - Protect natural environment and show compassion to creatures
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures.
plain_language: You should care for the environment by protecting forests, rivers, and wildlife, and treat animals with kindness.

title: Fundamental Duty - Develop scientific temper, humanism, and spirit of inquiry
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
plain_language: You should foster logical thinking, scientific curiosity, compassion for humanity, and a constant effort to improve society.

title: Fundamental Duty - Safeguard public property and abjure violence
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
plain_language: You must protect public infrastructure and property and reject the use of violence.

title: Fundamental Duty - Strive towards excellence in all spheres
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.
plain_language: You should work hard to excel in whatever you do so the country progresses overall.

title: Fundamental Duty - Provide educational opportunities for children aged 6 to 14
text: It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
plain_language: Parents and guardians must make sure their children aged 6 to 14 get to attend school.
